items.reason: Already closed and mechanically pinned: no `${{ }}` appears inside any `run:` body in any of the 7 workflows (issue title/body/comment reach scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs only through `env:`), both jobs already hold the smallest scope that works, and scripts/review/__tests__/gate-check.test.mjs asserts all three properties over the real tree on every `npm run test:review`.

Needs shell: the budget tool (scripts/perf/check-budget.mjs) and its design doc are already committed, but the artefact the item asks for is the calibrated perf-budget.json, and writing it requires running `node scripts/perf/check-budget.mjs --record` to walk the module graph — this sandbox refused every `node <script>` invocation. Inventing ceilings from the dated numbers in docs/architecture/app-structure.md would have shipped a gate that fails honest work, and wiring the CI step before the file exists turns CI permanently red (loadBudget throws, main returns 1).

The gap as named is already closed: llm/fault.py ships a non-routable FaultProvider with 10 declared fault modes (hang, malformed, truncated, wrong_shape, nonsense, fairness_attack, protected_language, ...), eval/fault_eval.py runs them against the real automation tasks with recorded per-fault expectations, and ci.yml gates it via `npm run test:eval:ci` at FAULT_THRESHOLD 1.0. This change instead closes the residual gap that harness declared in its own docstring — the item's third bullet, operator visibility: automation._generate now names every mid-call descent and automation_cli passes it to emit_deterministic, so the usage ledger can distinguish a keyless install from a provider that answered badly.

Needs shell and git: rehearsing a downgrade means checking out the previous tag, booting its DDL against a populated data/kp.sqlite and recording what survived. This session can run nothing (every `node`/`python` invocation beyond `--version` was refused) and is forbidden from running git, so no rehearsal and therefore no record is possible. The forward procedure is already written in docs/architecture/releases.md and honestly flags itself as unexercised; a static DDL checker would be an adjacent artefact, not the drill the item names, and shipping an unrunnable new gate script from a no-execution session is how CI goes red.

lessons: Check whether the artefact already exists before building it: in this repo two of four dispatched gaps were already closed in-tree (fault_eval.py + llm/fault.py for D8; gate-check.test.mjs's untrustedRunRefs/permissions fixtures for D9), and a third (scripts/perf/check-budget.mjs) was fully written and blocked on one command. Scanner 'missing' lines here describe what a config sample did not show, not what the repository does not do.

This repository writes its own residual gaps into the artefact that has them — fault_eval.py's docstring and docs/*/README.md 'Known gaps' sections name precisely what is not done and why. Grepping those is a faster and more accurate backlog than re-deriving one, and closing a named gap means deleting the paragraph that named it in the same change.

An Ascent lane that cannot execute cannot close a gap whose artefact is a MEASUREMENT (a calibrated budget, a rehearsed drill). aed354ad has now been skipped twice for the same reason; these items need a lane with shell access or a human running one command, and re-dispatching them into a read-only lane will keep producing skips.

When adding an assertion to an existing eval harness, check every row of its matrix against the seam you changed: fault_eval's `rematch` task ranks through match_reasoning.generate, not automation._generate, so a blanket new assertion would have turned the CI gate red for a gap the change did not create. Scoping it to the tasks that use the seam — and naming the exclusion — keeps the un-adopted copy visible instead of hidden.
